metaDescription: Five propane patio heater towers under $200 compared on BTU, burner build, tip-over protection, base weight and the real size of the warm circle.
expertTake: The Hykolity 50,000 BTU table-design tower is the best overall pick because it combines a stainless burner, a three-part safety system and a sturdy base. The Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU is the value pick with a known brand and a water-fillable base. Anyone with a small balcony or a covered porch should consider electric infrared instead of propane. Size to your seating, add ballast, and keep a spare cylinder, and any of these will serve a deck well. Keep a spare cylinder and a wind break, because those two things change an evening more than any difference between these towers.
introParagraphs: At this price the standard patio heater is a freestanding propane tower. A burner at the top, a reflector dome above it and a tank hidden in the base throw warmth in a circle around the post, and nothing in the electric world matches that reach on an open deck.
They are also tall, heavy and outdoor-only, which shapes how you buy and place one. The $200 cap reflects listing prices on the date this guide was updated, and prices move.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU propane patio heater, table design, wheels
products.description:
The Hykolity is a freestanding propane tower with a 50,000 BTU stainless steel burner, a table-style base that hides the tank and wheels for moving it. A triple protection system is described as covering tip-over and flame-out behaviour, which are the two failures that matter most with a tall gas heater. Ignition is by button and needs no battery.

Fifty thousand BTU per hour is roughly ten times the heat of a 1500 watt electric unit, and that is what lets it warm a circle of perhaps ten to fifteen feet across in calm air. On a windy night the effective circle shrinks, and the heater is wasted if the wind is strong. Compared with the Sweetcrispy, it is a little higher in output and has the table design that doubles as a shelf for drinks.

Ownership is about the tank and the surroundings. A 20 pound cylinder lasts roughly eight to ten hours on high, so keep a spare. Check connections for leaks with soapy water, keep the heater well away from overhead cover, awnings and umbrellas, and never use it indoors or in a garage. Store it under a cover. Assembly is the part many owners underestimate: expect an hour, two people and a flat patch of ground, and tighten the post sections before you connect the tank.
products.bestFor: Open decks and patios where reach matters.
pros: 50,000 BTU output warms a wide circle
cons: Tall and heavy without the tank
Gas only, never for enclosed spaces

products.name: Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU propane patio heater with wheels
products.description:
The Amazon Basics heater is a 46,000 BTU propane tower rated to warm up to a nine foot radius. It has a one-touch ignition button, an adjustable temperature knob and wheels, and its base can be filled with water to add weight and stability. It is sold for both residential and commercial use.

A nine foot radius is an honest, modest claim, a circle of about eighteen feet across, which suits a patio dining table better than a whole yard. The water-filled base is a practical stability feature, because a tall, light tower is the easiest thing in the garden to knock over. Compared with the Hykolity, it has less output but a known brand and a simpler design.

Keep a spare cylinder, check hoses for leaks and never place it under cover. Empty the water before winter storage so the base does not crack in frost. The water base is a clever feature, but it must be drained before frost and refilled before use. Do not light the heater without the base filled, since the lighter dry base is the tip risk the design is meant to fix. Keep the wheels locked once you have it where you want it.
products.bestFor: A dining table on a patio with predictable seating.
cons: Less output than the 50,000 BTU units

products.name: Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU propane patio heater, double-layer burner
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy puts a 48,000 BTU output behind a heavy double-layer 304 stainless steel burner mesh. The listing describes dual protection with automatic shutoff, and a wheeled base for moving. A double mesh burner is intended to resist the warping and burn-through that cheap single-layer burners suffer after a season or two.

It competes directly with the Hykolity and NEWBULIG. Output is about 4 percent lower than the Hykolity's 50,000 BTU, which is not a difference you will feel. The burner build is its argument, and in year three that is the part that fails first on cheap towers.

Treat it the same way: leak-check connections, keep it clear of overhead cover and cover it when not in use. In year three the stainless mesh is what separates a good tower from a tired one. Look for even blue flame across the whole burner, and if one side runs yellow, clean the burner ports and check the regulator. The wheels and the reflector dome are the next parts to inspect.
products.bestFor: Owners who care about burner longevity.

products.name: NEWBULIG 48,000 BTU propane patio heater, anti-tilt protection
products.description:
The NEWBULIG lists 48,000 BTU, a 304 stainless burner, 45 degree anti-tilt protection and flame-out protection. One-touch ignition and an adjustable flame cover everyday use. A side cutout and wheels make it easier to wheel to a new spot.

The safety listing is specific: a 45 degree tilt triggers shutoff, and flame-out protection stops gas if the flame dies. Against the Sweetcrispy the output is identical, so the choice is about details and price.

Check connections before every season, and store it dry. Like the others, it is worth wiping down the stainless after rain and keeping a spare igniter battery or a long match lighter on hand. If the flame goes out in a gust, wait a few minutes for gas to clear before relighting. Compare the regulator and hose quality when it arrives, since those are the parts that vary most between sellers. A hose with a stiff, cracked feel should be replaced before the first use.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want specific safety details listed.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU patio heater with sand box, conical barrel
products.description:
This Hykolity variant adds a sand box in the base and a conical barrel the listing says is more stable than a round design. Weight in the base is the cheapest way to keep a tall tower upright in a gust. It has the same 50,000 BTU output and double-layer stainless burner as its sibling.

The tradeoff is handling, since a sand-filled base is heavier to move. Compared with the table-design Hykolity, it is the one for windy decks.

Fill the sand box and keep it dry. With its extra weight it is not a heater you will move often, so place it once, level it with a bubble gauge and leave it in position for the season. It will store as a tall bulky item, so plan a spot in the garage. If you buy it, set it on a flat paver or concrete pad and not on loose gravel, because a soft base negates the weight advantage.
products.bestFor: Windy decks where stability comes first.

buyingCriteria.criterion: BTU is output, radius is reach
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 50,000 BTU tower like the Hykolity warms roughly a ten to fifteen foot circle in calm air, while the Amazon Basics claims a nine foot radius for 46,000 BTU. Compare the claimed radius and your seating, not just the headline BTU. For a six-person table on a 12 foot deck, one 50,000 BTU tower is plenty; for a 20 foot party space you will want two placed apart. Owners often find the first night warmer than expected and the tenth night colder, because they forget to move the tower closer as the group shifts.

A tall tower is easy to knock over. Look for tip-over shutoff, like the NEWBULIG's 45 degree anti-tilt, and flame-out protection that stops gas flow if the flame dies. Wind above a light breeze cuts the warm circle sharply, so a wall or screen on the windy side helps more than extra BTU. Ask yourself whether a wind break is possible; a simple screen can double the useful circle.

The Amazon Basics base fills with water and the Hykolity sand-box model fills with sand. Added weight is the cheapest stability feature. Always check the minimum overhead clearance in the manual, which is commonly several feet above the reflector. A low flame all evening is cheaper and quieter than a high flame for an hour.

A double-layer 304 stainless burner like the Sweetcrispy's resists warping. Burners are the part that fails first on cheap towers. Run the burner on a lower setting once you are warm, because it stretches a cylinder and lowers noise. Keep children and pets outside the reflector radius, because the dome and post stay hot after shutoff.

A 20 pound cylinder lasts roughly eight to ten hours on high. Keep a spare and use the lowest setting that keeps you comfortable. Do not move a lit heater, and let it cool before moving or covering it. A cover protects the igniter and burner, which are the parts rain damages first.

Gas heaters are for open air only. Keep them clear of overhead cover, awnings and umbrellas, and never use one indoors or in a garage. Store the cylinder outside, upright and away from heat, and never in a closed space. If a gas smell is present, shut the valve and move away before checking anything.

specDecoder.meaning: Heat output per hour. Heat per hour, not warmth you feel.
How far warmth reaches from the post. The circle you can sit in.
A switch that cuts gas if the tower leans. A cutoff when the heater leans too far.
A valve that stops gas if the flame goes out. It stops gas if the flame dies.
A corrosion-resistant steel grade. A grade that resists rust.

howToChoose.note: Measure the seating circle first, because a tower is only useful if everyone sits within its radius.
Prices move, so read these tiers as relative positions.

cards.label: Water
cards.text: The Amazon Basics fills with water, which is easy to drain and add.

cards.label: Sand
cards.text: The Hykolity sand-box model adds heavier ballast but is harder to move.

howToChoose.note: Pick water for ease; sand for wind. If you cannot decide, pick the one whose base matches your wind exposure, since stability matters more than a small difference in output.
Safety listings should be specific, since vague claims tell you little.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High BTU, a stable base and tilt shutoff.

howToChoose.note: Consider placing the heater against a wind break to keep the warm circle intact.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a better finish or higher output for a large area.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only warm a dining table. The Amazon Basics is enough.

howToChoose.note: Spending more usually buys finish and materials, not a bigger warm circle, so decide whether you will notice the difference over several seasons.

maintenance.why: Gas leaks are the most serious risk. Do it with soapy water and look for bubbles. Skipping this task is how small leaks go unnoticed for a whole season.
Debris causes uneven flame. Use a soft brush and avoid poking the ports. Look for uneven flame as a sign of a dirty burner.
Cracks signal replacement. Replace any hose with cracks or stiffness. A cracked hose is cheap to replace and expensive to ignore.
Water or sand keeps it stable. Refill after rain or evaporation. Rain and evaporation lower the weight faster than you expect.
Rain damages the igniter. Remove the cylinder first. A dry, covered spot protects the igniter.

faq.q: How big a circle does it warm?
faq.a: Roughly ten to fifteen feet across in calm air for 50,000 BTU. Propane suits big open spaces, while infrared suits small or windy ones.

faq.q: How long does a tank last?
faq.a: Roughly eight to ten hours on high for a 20 pound cylinder. A cylinder swap is a normal part of owning one, so keep a spare filled.
No. Gas heaters are for open air only. Never use a gas heater inside a tent, garage, carport or enclosed porch.

faq.q: Can I use it under a pergola?
faq.a: Only with the clearance the manual states. Pergolas with solid roofs are not suitable unless the manual explicitly allows it.
Yes, wind shrinks the warm circle. If the warm circle feels small, move the heater closer to the seating, not the other way round.

faq.q: Do I need to assemble it?
faq.a: Yes, plan an hour. Plan on an hour to assemble and a second person to help lift the post. If you are unsure about a gas heater, ask a local propane supplier to check the connection during a refill.
